description: Build the production-grade backend API layer between customers and Dokploy. Yalla Control Plane is the source of truth for tenants, ownership, policy, limits, desired state, audit, and provisioning jobs; Dokploy is the private execution engine used for infrastructure provisioning.

sourceApi.title: Dokploy API
sourceApi.role: Private provisioning backend only; customers must not call this API directly.

productPrinciples: The CLI, control-plane API, and worker live in the same Go repository as separate binaries so shared contracts do not drift.
Yalla Control Plane is the source of truth; Dokploy is the provisioning engine.
Customers, agents, and CI must never receive broad Dokploy API keys.
The backend mirrors Dokploy hierarchy: Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service.
Authorization, ownership, limits, audit, and desired state are enforced before any Dokploy operation.
Expose intent-based Yalla APIs, not a customer-facing generic Dokploy proxy.
Dokploy permissions may be configured as defense-in-depth, but Yalla policy is authoritative.
Every public API response, error code, audit event, and state transition is a compatibility contract.
No MVP shortcuts. The backend must include migrations, tests, observability, security controls, and operational runbooks.
Pricing is enforced through plan entitlements, quotas, and billing-grade usage counters, not through frontend-only package text.
Traffic and infrastructure metering must be owned by Yalla; Dokploy monitoring is useful operational input but not the billing source of truth.
Current resource state is used for real-time quota enforcement; append-only usage events and period counters are used for billing and growth tracking.
All pricing, entitlement, metering, usage aggregation, billing export, quota, and enforcement settings must be configurable from the backoffice/admin API with audit trails.
Runtime pricing and metering behavior must come from database-backed configuration, not hardcoded constants, except for safe built-in defaults and migration seeds.

architecture.apiFramework: net/http with chi-style routing; keep handlers thin and logic in internal/controlplane packages
architecture.database: PostgreSQL via pgx; migrations through goose or atlas; SQL must be tenant-scoped and testable
architecture.queue: Postgres-backed durable jobs, preferably river or a small SKIP LOCKED implementation
architecture.dokploy: Typed Dokploy provisioning client behind internal/controlplane/dokploy; never exposed to customers as raw proxy

repositoryTopology.reason: The existing CLI already integrates with Dokploy. Keeping the backend in the same module lets the CLI, API, and worker reuse Dokploy client behavior, stable envelopes, typed errors, ID conventions, test utilities, and release/version metadata.
repositoryTopology.rule: Future CLI customer workflows should call the Yalla Control Plane API by default; raw Dokploy access remains an explicit internal/admin escape hatch only.
repositoryTopology.internalPackageReason: Go internal packages are private to this repository/module. Backend implementation code lives under internal/controlplane so external modules cannot import it as an SDK and so the HTTP API remains the public boundary.
boundaries: cmd/yalla is the CLI binary and should depend on internal/cli plus a control-plane HTTP client when customer workflows move to the backend.
cmd/yalla-api is the backend HTTP API binary and depends on internal/controlplane packages.
cmd/yalla-worker is the backend worker binary and depends on internal/controlplane worker/job/provisioning packages.
internal/cli owns Cobra commands, terminal UX, local config, and CLI output behavior.
internal/controlplane owns backend API handlers, auth, policy, quota, jobs, persistence, metering, billing, audit, and provisioning orchestration.
internal/api and internal/dokploy are shared low-level Dokploy integration packages used behind explicit boundaries.
The CLI must not import internal/controlplane/store, policy, quota, jobs, or worker packages directly for customer workflows; it should call the control-plane API through an HTTP client.
If a reusable external Go SDK is needed later, create pkg/yallaapi or a generated client package rather than exporting backend internals.

futureClientPackage.publicLater: pkg/yallaapi only if external Go consumers need a supported SDK

technologyStack.http: net/http, chi-compatible router, middleware chain, typed handlers
technologyStack.database: PostgreSQL, pgx, migrations with goose or atlas, optional sqlc for typed queries
technologyStack.queue: Postgres-backed jobs; no Redis dependency required for v1 backend
technologyStack.auth: Hashed API keys, service accounts, session/JWT verifier, scoped grants, RBAC policy engine
technologyStack.secrets: Envelope encryption abstraction for secret variables and Dokploy service token handling
technologyStack.observability: Structured JSON logs, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, request IDs, audit events
technologyStack.metering: Traefik metrics for HTTP traffic, Prometheus-compatible time-series storage for raw metrics, Yalla usage_events and usage_counters for billing-grade aggregation
technologyStack.billing: Internal billing provider abstraction; Stripe/manual invoicing adapters can be added without changing entitlement or usage models

userStories.notes: Added runtime.RunHTTPServer (context-cancellation driven graceful shutdown bounded by a fresh timeout context) and runtime.Readiness (concurrency-safe named startup gates). httpapi.NewHandler now takes a ReadinessReporter; /readyz returns 503 + yalla.error.v1 E_SERVER until gates pass, 200 + yalla.output.v1 once ready. New worker.Loop stops claiming jobs as soon as its context is cancelled and releases interrupted in-flight leases on a shutdown-independent context; worker.NoopClaimer is the placeholder until the durable job store lands. Config gained YALLA_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT (per-profile defaults, 1s-5m range validation). cmd/yalla-api and cmd/yalla-worker wired to the new lifecycle helpers. Tests cover readiness transitions, cancellation, shutdown-timeout bounding, serve errors, in-flight lease release, and completed-job non-release. gofmt, go build, go vet, go test ./..., and go test -race ./... pass. goimports/golangci-lint/staticcheck/govulncheck not installed locally. userStories.notes: internal/controlplane/policy is a pure, total decision engine: Engine.Decide(Principal, Action, Resource) -> Decision{Allow, Reason} with stable Reason codes, and Engine.Authorize / AuthorizeCtx map denials onto typed apierr (Unauthenticated/Forbidden) for handlers and store units of work. Six built-in roles (owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support) plus a CustomRoleResolver hook map to a small capability set (self/read/deploy/write/admin/owner/support); the 61-action catalog maps every API-surface requiredAction to one capability. Scoped Grants narrow and widen authority within an org via Scope containment over Organization->Project->Environment->Service; cross-tenant resources are denied by construction except support reads/break-glass. WithPrincipal/PrincipalFromContext carry the principal on the request context. TestPolicyMatrix exhaustively covers all 6 roles x 61 actions; tests also cover no-principal, disabled, unknown action/role, custom roles, grant narrowing/widening/ignored-invalid, cross-tenant, scope containment, apierr mapping with no ID leakage, and the context carrier. gofmt, go build, go vet, go test ./..., and go test -race ./... all pass. Postgres integration criterion is N/A (pure engine, no persistence); DB-backed grant rows land with the grants-persistence story. JSON-envelope criterion is N/A (no HTTP surface yet); the engine returns typed apierr that the existing apienvelope renderer already maps.

userStories.notes: internal/controlplane/httpapi/api_keys_list_policy_test.go drives the real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() through every built-in role (owner/admin allow via ReasonAllowedByRole; developer/viewer/ci/support deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — keys.read is CapAdmin), through revoked/expired credentials (Disabled principal -> ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled), through a wrong-organization principal (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant; the load-bearing assertion: support is NOT a cross-tenant exception for keys.read because CapAdmin is excluded from the engine's cross-tenant clause; bonus: support cannot list keys of its own home org either — ReasonDeniedNoCapability), and through scoped grant containment (project/env/service-scoped admin grants all denied keys.read on the org root via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, sibling project / production env / parent env-write all denied at the engine, organization-level admin grant allowed via ReasonAllowedByGrant, organization-level viewer grant denied — pinning CapAdmin against the grant path; cross-tenant {org_id} on a scoped key still 403 ReasonDeniedCrossTenant). All deny paths assert the reader is never reached and the body never echoes the seeded key id/prefix or the principal/org/member id.

userStories.notes: Implemented GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits. Returns effective quota limits resolved as organization override beats plan default in one SQL statement; wire fields are resource, limit_value, enforcement_mode, source ('organization' or 'plan_default'). Resources with no policy at either scope are omitted. New store.LimitsReader composes QuotaRepository.ListEffectiveLimits through Store.Read with a pluggable PlanLookup (DefaultPlan fallback). Action limits.read authorized via organizationIDResolver against {org_id}; reader-port pattern threaded NewHandler -> newRouteTable -> handler closure. Contract tests cover success, empty list, path-org_id forwarding, 401 unauthenticated, 403 cross-tenant, 503 store outage, and nil-reader internal error. Store integration tests cover precedence resolution, empty result, tenant scoping, default vs custom PlanLookup, and nil-store rejection.

userStories.notes: Implemented: PATCH /v1/organizations/{org_id}/limits upserts organization-scoped quota policies. Request body: {limits:[{resource,limit_value,enforcement_mode?}, ...]} validated by httpapi (missing limit_value -> 400) and by the store layer (closed-set resource, non-negative limit, closed-set mode, no duplicates). Required action limits.write (CapAdmin, no support cross-tenant exception). Store-layer LimitsService composes a tenant existence pre-check (typed NotFound on missing org), one organization-scoped quota_policies upsert per entry, an immutable audit record (action=limits.write, metadata.updated_resources=sorted closed-set names), and an in-tx re-read of effective limits — all in one Store.Write. New QuotaRepository.UpsertOrganizationPolicy uses ON CONFLICT (organization_id, resource) WHERE scope_kind='organization' to target the partial unique index. Wired through NewHandler/newRouteTable as a new LimitsUpdater port; the route uses organizationIDResolver so cross-tenant {org_id} is a 403 before the handler runs. cmd/yalla-api builds the LimitsService at startup.

userStories.notes: Added internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_delete_policy_test.go: four tests driving real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() against the production request path. Roles matrix (Owner/Admin/Developer allow via ReasonAllowedByRole at 202 Accepted with the canonical scheduled-deletion row; Viewer/CI/Support deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability at 403 — CapWrite is OUTSIDE the support cross-tenant exception). Revoked/expired Disabled keys deny via ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled. Wrong-organization principal surfaces as 404 NotFound at the persistence boundary (deleter called with attacker home org, never the victim's) AND every role denies cross-tenant via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant at the engine. Grant containment: project-target Admin allowed, project-sibling Admin denied OutOfScope, project-VIEWER denied NoCapability, env-scope denied OutOfScope (with explicit staging→production denial proof), service-scope denied OutOfScope (with sibling-service and parent-env denial), org-Admin allowed, org-Viewer denied NoCapability, and a foreign-home grantee denied. Every deny path proves the deleter was never reached and the body never echoes the canonical project's id/slug/display name. gofmt, go vet, go build, go test ./..., go test -race ./... all pass.

pricingAndUsageTracking.strategy: Start with quota-enforced plans plus append-only usage events and period counters. Hard-limit countable resources immediately; meter growth-sensitive traffic and infrastructure usage before billing or overage enforcement becomes strict.

concepts: plan_entitlements define included usage and hard/soft limits
subscriptions attach an organization to a plan and billing period
subscription_entitlements override plan defaults for add-ons, migrations, and enterprise contracts
usage_events record what happened over time
quota_reservations prevent concurrent over-allocation before provisioning completes
billing_exports send accepted metered usage to Stripe or a manual invoicing adapter later

features: dedicated Dokploy organization or instance option

dokploy.role: Operational input for server/container/app metrics where available; not treated as the only billing source of truth.

traefik.role: Primary HTTP traffic source for RPS, request count, status-code counts, latency, and bandwidth attribution.

yallaEvents.role: Authoritative product events for deployments, build minutes, resource lifecycle, reservations, and billing-period counters.

infrastructureCollectors.role: Storage and container-resource source when Dokploy metrics are insufficient.
examples: Docker stats or cAdvisor for CPU/RAM
node exporter or volume scanner for disk and volume usage

attributionRules: Yalla controls Dokploy app/service names and must include stable service IDs such as yalla-svc_456 where possible.
Metrics are attributed by mapping Traefik service labels or Dokploy app names to dokploy_refs, then to service, environment, project, and organization.
Every aggregated usage counter must be org-scoped and include the source, period, unit, and aggregation version.
Billing-grade counters must be derived from append-only usage_events or reproducible metric windows, never from mutable current state alone.
Current resource state is still used for real-time quota checks such as active services, active databases, domains, and members.

backofficeConfiguration.goal: The backoffice is the operational control surface for plans, entitlements, subscriptions, metering sources, usage aggregation, billing exports, quota policies, feature flags, and enforcement modes. Backend services read effective configuration from Postgres-backed admin state with safe caching and audit logs.
configurableResources: organization subscription status and billing period
metering source configuration for Traefik, Prometheus, Dokploy, cAdvisor, Docker stats, volume scanners, and backup metadata
metric attribution rules and quarantine policy
usage aggregation schedules and period close rules
billing provider adapters and export settings
feature flags by plan, organization, project, environment, or service
admin/break-glass roles and support access policy
safetyRules: Every backoffice mutation requires admin authorization and is audited with before/after diffs.
Backoffice changes support dry-run validation before publish.
Dangerous changes can be scheduled for a future effective_at timestamp.
Published changes create immutable versions so invoices and historical usage can be reproduced.
Secrets in metering source or billing provider config are write-only and encrypted at rest.
Backoffice APIs must support rollback to a previous published version where safe.

  Admin["Backoffice admin"] --> API["Admin API"]

  Draft --> Validate["Dry-run validation"]
  Validate --> Publish["Publish effective config"]
  Publish --> Audit[("Audit log")]
  Publish --> Cache["Config cache invalidation"]
  Cache --> Runtime["API / worker / aggregator runtime"]

  Defaults["Safe built-in defaults"] --> Seeds["Migration seed config"]
  Seeds --> Backoffice["Published backoffice config"]
  Backoffice --> Overrides["Org/subscription overrides"]
  Overrides --> Effective["Effective runtime config"]
  Effective --> API["API enforcement"]
  Effective --> Worker["Worker provisioning"]

  Effective --> Billing["Billing export"]
